## My thinking

I have about 8 mu of land, same as always. My father grew wheat and corn on this land, and his father before him. That's what I grow. There is no question about it. The wheat goes in around October after the summer corn comes off, and the corn goes back in after the wheat harvest in June. Same rotation, every year. That's how everyone here does it.

I'll buy seed from the village supply shop like I always do. The shop only sells the improved varieties now anyway — nobody sells the old seeds anymore. I'll get Jimai wheat and probably Xianyu hybrid corn. Those work fine. My neighbor used Xianyu 335 last year and did well.

For fertilizer, I put down a good amount before planting and top-dress later. More fertilizer means better stalks and fuller grain, that's what I've seen with my own eyes over thirty years. I spread urea and the compound fertilizer bag from the shop. I don't measure exactly — I just know how heavy to spread.

For water, I pump from my well three times for wheat: once before winter sets in hard, once when the stalks start shooting up, once when the heads come out. For corn I pump maybe twice — once early if it's dry, once when it tassels. The well is getting harder to pump every year but I still manage.

I spray for weeds after the wheat emerges, then spray again in spring for aphids when I see them. For corn I spray once for borers. I don't spray if I don't see a problem — the chemicals cost money.

Tillage I do rotary, same as my neighbors. No deep plow, that's more fuel and more work.
